extraction.name: CADS (Comprehensive Anatomical Dataset and Segmentation)
extraction.description: CADS is a large-scale, open-source dataset for whole-body CT segmentation comprising 22,022 CT volumes with complete annotations for 167 anatomical structures spanning from head to knees. The dataset aggregates images from over 40 sources including public archives (TCIA, NLST, CT-RATE, AbdomenCT-1K), medical imaging challenges, and newly contributed hospital data (484 head CTs from Istanbul Medipol University and 586 triphasic contrast-enhanced abdominal CT scans from TUM). The collection spans over 100 medical centers across 16 countries, collected between 2007 and 2024, covering healthy subjects and various pathological conditions including cancers, COVID-19, and traumatic injuries. Only 21% of the scans originally contained partial annotations; the rest were generated via an automated pseudo-labeling pipeline with shape-based quality control and multi-strategy label optimization.
extraction.license: Mixed (varies per source dataset, including CC BY 3.0, CC BY 4.0, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, CC BY-SA 4.0, CC BY-NC 4.0, CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, CC-BY-SA-NC, and restricted licenses)
extraction.creator: Murong Xu, Tamaz Amiranashvili, Fernando Navarro, et al. (University of Zurich, ETH Zurich, Technical University of Munich, and collaborators)
extraction.citeAs: Xu, M., Amiranashvili, T., Navarro, F., et al. (2025). CADS: A Comprehensive Anatomical Dataset and Segmentation for Whole-Body Anatomy in Computed Tomography. arXiv:2507.22953.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The CADS-dataset aggregates 22,022 CT volumes from 40 diverse sources through three main channels: (1) large-scale public archives including TotalSegmentator, NLST, CT-RATE, and AbdomenCT-1K; (2) specialized annotation collections from medical imaging challenges (Grand Challenge, MICCAI) and focused research studies (Han-Seg, SAROS, TCIA); and (3) newly contributed images and annotations including manual annotations of critical OARs on VISCERAL, 484 newly acquired anonymized head CTs from Istanbul Medipol University, and 586 triphasic contrast-enhanced abdominal CT scans from TUM Klinikum Rechts der Isar.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Document analysis, Manual Human Curator, Physical data collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Only 4,695 of 22,022 CT volumes (21%) contained partial manual annotations from public sources; the remaining 79% lacked any annotations. Annotations were typically confined to a single organ system, motivating the automated pseudo-labeling approach.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw CT volumes obtained from 40+ sources including TCIA, Grand Challenge, MICCAI challenges, TotalSegmentator, NLST, CT-RATE, AbdomenCT-1K, VISCERAL, Han-Seg, SAROS, and newly acquired hospital data from Istanbul Medipol University (head CTs) and TUM Klinikum Rechts der Isar (abdominal CTs).
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Facial features in newly acquired hospital head CT scans were anonymized using a Gaussian filter (σ = 5 voxels at 1.5mm spacing) to preserve patient privacy while maintaining structural integrity for anatomical analysis. Sparse 2D slice-based annotations in SAROS were interpolated to create dense 3D per-slice annotations. Rib segmentation was refined to retrieve costovertebral joints using vesselFM.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Three-step standardization pipeline: (1) reorient all images to RAS (Right-Anterior-Superior) convention, (2) resample to uniform 1.5mm isotropic resolution to balance segmentation accuracy with computational efficiency, and (3) simplify original affine transformation matrices by removing rotation and translation components while preserving only scaling and shear.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Multi-stage annotation methodology: (1) Target structures organized into 9 anatomical groups with specialized models trained per group using high-quality annotations from established datasets (TotalSegmentator, VISCERAL, Han-Seg, SAROS); (2) Whole-body pseudo-labeling propagates annotations across unlabeled scans using nnU-Net framework; (3) Automated quality control using neural implicit functions for shape-based outlier detection (excluding bottom 10% by Hausdorff distance); (4) Multi-strategy label generation through ensemble selection combining three complementary 'flavors' (GT-flavor, Pseudo-flavor, Shape-flavor); (5) Structure-specific refinements including rib segmentation correction preserving costovertebral joints. Manual annotations were contributed by three in-house medical research assistants and a radiation oncologist for the VISCERAL Gold Corpus.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: nnU-Net framework; vesselFM foundation model for tubular structure detection; ANTS for non-rigid registration; SimNIBS MRI atlas for brain registration; 3D Slicer for clinical deployment
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Statistical ranking process for selecting the best performing model flavor per anatomical structure using Dice Similarity Coefficient (primary) and 95% Hausdorff distance (secondary). Statistical tests applied include Shapiro-Wilk (normality), Levene's (variance equality), ANOVA/Welch's ANOVA/Kruskal-Wallis, with post-hoc Tukey's HSD or Dunn's tests at p<0.05 significance threshold. Expert radiation oncologist conducted systematic slice-by-slice review on 2,864 patients from University Hospital Zurich, evaluating geometric accuracy, anatomical completeness, and adherence to consensus organ-at-risk delineation practices.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Three in-house medical research assistants and one radiation oncologist (J.C.P.) for VISCERAL Gold Corpus annotations. Clinical validation led by an experienced radiation oncologist with 5.5 years of practice. Additional review by in-house medical professionals for TotalSegmentator test set quality assessment.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: nnU-Net framework (residual encoder UNet, version 2.5.1); vesselFM foundation model for tubular/rib structure detection; ANTS non-rigid transformation; neural implicit functions (auto-decoder) for shape-based quality control; PyTorch 2.5.1 with CUDA 12.4; Seg-metrics and surface-distance packages for evaluation; TPTBox Python library for postprocessing
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Dataset publicly available via Hugging Face (https://huggingface.co/datasets/mrmrx/CADS-dataset); trained models and codebase at https://github.com/murong-xu/CADS; 3D Slicer plugin at https://github.com/murong-xu/SlicerCADS. SNOMED-CT terminology integration for healthcare infrastructure compatibility.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: CT scans include patient age (≥18 years for Istanbul Medipol University head CTs), pathological conditions, and geographic origin across 16 countries. Facial features in newly acquired head CT scans are intentionally anonymized using Gaussian filtering to preserve patient privacy. Study received ethical approval from institutional review boards at Istanbul Medipol University and Technical University of Munich.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The framework aims to advance robust AI solutions in radiology and make comprehensive anatomical analysis accessible to clinicians and researchers. Clinical potential spans radiation oncology (streamlined treatment planning), diagnostic radiology (automated organ quantification), and research (large-scale population studies). The 3D Slicer plugin lowers accessibility barriers for healthcare practitioners without technical expertise.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Geographic bias toward certain countries (16 countries, over 100 medical centers, concentrated in Europe, North America, and parts of Asia). Limited training data for certain structures (e.g., buccal mucosa in less than 1,000 scans with only 30 ground-truth annotations). Class imbalance across 167 structures, with uppermost cervical vertebrae (C1-C5) appearing less frequently. Known systematic errors identified in existing TotalSegmentator annotations for complex structures like ribs and vertebrae.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Limitations include: (1) shape-based quality assessment excludes potentially valuable pathological cases with atypical anatomical variations; (2) coverage limited to head-to-knees, excluding hands and feet; (3) certain structures require refinement - brain mask is overly inclusive, optic chiasm tends to be under-segmented, heart segmentation omits superior portions, rectum appears shorter than anatomical extent, trachea limited to air content; (4) facial features are anonymized, limiting applications requiring detailed facial analysis; (5) very small organs (volumes below 0.5 mL) like arytenoid cartilage have accuracy limited by CT resolution and partial volume effects; (6) anatomically complex small glands present challenges.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Primary use cases: Training, Testing, Validation for whole-body CT segmentation models. Clinical applications: precise radiation planning in radiation oncology, region-specific abnormality detection, automated localization of metastases, body composition analysis through tissue quantification, longitudinal organ tracking, personalized anatomical modeling, large-scale population studies. Technical research: anatomical landmark detection, cross-modality registration (CT-MRI fusion, PET-CT alignment), anatomy-guided image synthesis and reconstruction for radiation dose reduction.
